topic: National competition for Integra Dental Design: dentist-facing shipping labs (Glidewell, Dandy, NDX, DDS, Modern/MicroDental, ROE, etc.), lab-to-lab milling centers (Monster, Alien, Haus, Argen, Strategy, etc.), dentist lab-switching evidence, and the DSO in-house/preferred-lab trend
summary:
Method note: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before this task started, so discovery ran on Exa search and all primary pages were read with Exa fetch. All access dates are 2026-10-12; page dates are given where shown.

FACTS, most consequential first.

1. Glidewell is the price and speed anchor, and it undercuts Integra on every commodity line. Glidewell's live price list (glidewell.com/price-list, undated, accessed 2026-10-12) shows BruxZir Full-Strength at $109 analog / $89 model-free digital, BruxZir Esthetic $119/$99, e.max posterior $129/$109, titanium custom abutment $318/$298, BruxZir crown + custom abutment $454 (minus $40 digital = $414), BruxZir screw-retained $339 (minus $20 digital = $319), and three digital full-arch tiers: Complete Service $2,795 (Esthetic $2,995), Copy Service $1,695, and direct Mill Service from a provided file $1,450 (Esthetic $1,650). Analog full-arch is $3,433, or $4,150 with a titanium bar; the screw-retained hybrid denture (milled Ti bar + denture) is $2,335; a milled implant bar/framework is $923. Monolithic BruxZir is 3 days in lab; Next-Day BruxZir (digital, scan by 2 p.m.) includes free shipping. Shipping otherwise is FedEx overnight $9 each way per box or free USPS Priority (2–4 days). BruxZir carries a lifetime warranty with a no-fault remake policy, and Glidewell will replace any other lab's fractured monolithic zirconia crown free. Against this, Integra's $129 FCZ is 45% above Glidewell's digital price, its $149 e.max is 37% above, and its $269–$299 implant-crown package is roughly at parity with Glidewell's $319 digital screw-retained price. Integra's $1,700 monolithic arch is $1,095 below Glidewell's Complete Service but only $250 above Glidewell's dentist-facing mill-from-file price.

2. Dandy sells a scanner-plus-lab subscription, not a fee schedule. Its pricing page (meetdandy.com/pricing) states a $1,000/month lab minimum for a free Dandy Vision scanner or $2,500/month for a TRIOS 5, month-to-month, free remakes, lifetime warranty on fixed work, free shipping, and a DSO tier with a free scanner per location. Per-unit fees are only partially public: zirconia "from $99," dentures from $199/arch, surgical guides $109/site, night guards from $59 bundled (Dandy labs page), and $398 list for an all-in implant restoration (Dandy implant page, offer dated to April 30, 2026). A third-party review (Peak Dental Studio, May 2026) reports e.max from $125. Fixed work is made in Utah, removables in Texas; Dandy accepts no physical impressions.

3. Lab-to-lab milling is a $19–$35 zirconia crown market with free shipping at low thresholds, so Bear Milling's $22 is at parity, not a discount. Monster Milling (Plano TX) lists Honorzir HT+ crowns at $19, implant crowns $35, Ti custom abutments from $65, a flat $350 Ti bar, full-arch zirconia from $580, Bar+Zir $950, 1-day crown milling from STL, no minimum, and free ground shipping on orders of $90+. Alien Milling (Glendora CA) lists Alien HT solid zirconia at $22, Multi-Layer 2.0 $34, implant crown $48, a flat $399 Ti bar, and full-arch hybrid zirconia at $649 (HT) to $1,049. Haus (Carrollton TX) lists crowns at $18–$35. Bear's $650 full-arch from STL sits against Monster $580, Alien $649 and K&A/Backup $650; Bear's $299 Ti bar is below Alien $399 and Monster $350 (which adds $280–$400 if Monster designs).

4. Switching behavior is well documented and stable. The LMT/Dental Economics dentist survey (LMT, Mar 2019) found 46% of dentists switched their primary lab in the prior five years, 71% because of inconsistent work, with price a factor for only about a third, and 44% found their new lab via a colleague referral. LMT's top-10 chart shows inconsistent quality 68%, poor communication 30%, late cases 26%, Rx not followed 21%, lower fees 5%. ADA's 2008 lab survey found the average GP uses three labs (90.3% use two or more; 2.8% have in-office labs). Dentaltown's 2023 poll (n=165) found 56% use two or fewer labs, 37% three to five, and 38% fired a lab in the prior 12 months. LMT's 2024 Remake Survey puts average external remakes at 2.5% (C&B) and 2.2% (implants), with labs attributing 82% of remakes to dentist error.

5. DSO consolidation redirects lab spend toward preferred networks, not toward in-house C&B labs. ADA HPI data (via IDT, Oct 2025) show DSO affiliation rising from 7.2% (2015) to 16.1% (2024); US labs with payroll fell 25.8% from 6,865 (2013) to 5,096 (2023); NADL's Spring 2025 survey attributes 65% of lab sales to solo practices and only 8% to DSOs. Heartland runs "Diamond Trusted Labs" (Leixir through 2029, DDS Lab since 2008) and reports remakes under 3% and roughly $190/arch savings versus local labs; Aspen operates onsite denture labs and trained 1,300+ technicians (Feb 2025). Glidewell opened a DSO-only BruxZir Express lab in Memphis (Apr 2025). Local to Integra: NDX Issaquah (640 NW Gilman Blvd) and Modern Dental Center Seattle (330 112th Ave NE, Bellevue) are national-network labs in Integra's own market.

ESTIMATES. GP lab spend: ADA HPI 2025 gross billings average $965,660; HPI does not publish the lab-expense category, and third-party benchmarks range 5–10% of collections, implying roughly $40k–$80k/year per GP owner. Chairside mill penetration: no authoritative 2025 figure; Dentaltown 2023 self-selected poll shows 23% "already provide crowns in office"; digital impression use was 57% in 2024 (IDT). Working estimate 10–20% of GPs own a mill.

UNKNOWNS. Dandy's full fee schedule, NDX/Modern/MicroDental current pricing, Burbank/Sun/Bayshore/ProSmile/Dental Lab Direct/Absolute fee schedules, and Argen/Core3d/Jensen/Zahn/Preat/Panthera/Zirkonzahn milling prices are quote- or login-only. The Harmony Dental "left Dandy" story is Integra's own account and was not independently verified; Dandy's public record is mixed (Dentaltown 2025 summary; 3.6/5 on 63 Google reviews for the Lehi lab) rather than uniformly negative.

findings.claim: 46% of dentists switched their primary lab in the prior five years; inconsistent quality was the #1 reason (71%), price a distant second (~1/3)
findings.detail: LMT/Dental Economics joint dentist survey. Delayed turnaround/late cases and Rx not followed tied for third. 44% found their new lab through a referral from another dentist; dentists also respond to in-person sales calls and samples. Top features sought in a new lab: high-quality work, good communication, reasonable prices, in that order. Half of dentists had NOT switched in five years.
findings.value: 46% switched in 5 yrs; 71% inconsistent work; ~33% price; 44% referral

findings.claim: LMT 'Top 10 reasons dentists switch laboratories' chart: inconsistent quality 68%, poor relationship/communication 30%, delayed turnaround 26%, Rx not followed 21%, lower fees only 5%
findings.detail: Multiple responses allowed. Other reasons: lab could not meet changing technical needs 9%; lab closed 9%; price increase 8%; followed a key technician 6%; no problems, just wanted to try another lab 3%. Chart derived from the LMT/DE dentist survey series (2011/2013).

findings.claim: 61% of dentists had switched labs at least once in the prior 10 years (2011); poor occlusion was the most common technical problem
findings.detail: LMT/Dental Economics 2011 survey. About a third also noted incorrect shades, failure to follow the prescription, and restorations that fit the model but not the mouth.

findings.claim: 49% of dentists changed labs in five years (2013); 56% consistently use three labs, only 13% rely on one; 17% had a digital impression system; 63% neither had nor planned chairside CAD/CAM
findings.detail: Dental Economics + LMT survey of 200 dentists (65% practicing 20+ years, 66% solo). Nearly half of switchers switched only once; 17% twice, 8% three times, 3% more. Reasons: inconsistent quality/technical problems first, then high prices, delayed turnaround, poor communication, Rx not followed.
findings.value: 49% switched; 56% use 3 labs; 13% use 1 lab; 17% IOS

findings.claim: ADA 2008 Survey on the Use of Dental Labs: average dentist uses 3 labs (range 1–9); 90.3% use two or more; 77.8% use 2–4; 12.5% use 5+; 2.8% have an in-office lab
findings.detail: 91.1% used independent labs in their primary practice; 6.1% used none. 84.4% of respondents were GPs. Of the 31 respondents with in-office labs, 67.7% did it because volume made it feasible, 45.2% wanted an in-office technician, 38.7% were dissatisfied with outside quality.

findings.claim: Dentaltown poll (Aug 19–Sep 20, 2023): 56% of dentists use two or fewer labs regularly, 37% three to five, 7% more than five; 38% fired or stopped using a lab in the past 12 months
findings.detail: n=165 for lab count, n=102 for firing question; self-selected Dentaltown members. Same poll: 42% speak with their lab tech weekly; 61% use zirconia on second molars more than 50% of the time; 23% 'already provide crowns in office' (n=105); 44% perceive a reduction in lab quality since the pandemic; 69% have delivered neither printed nor milled dentures.
findings.value: 56% <=2 labs; 38% fired a lab in 12 mo; 23% in-office crowns

findings.claim: Dentaltown 2003 poll (historical, n≈360–547): lab expense as % of total overhead clustered at 7–10%; 60% cited inconsistent work as the primary reason for dropping a lab, 22% poor fit; 41% chose their lab for quality vs 3% for price
findings.detail: Lab expense share of overhead: 5–6% (23%), 7–8% (29%), 9–10% (29%), 11–12% (10%), 13%+ (9%). 45% said their most-used lab charged $101–150/unit (2003 dollars). 45% expect <1% remake rate and 44% expect 2–3% as the standard for 'consistent quality'. 83% send 61%+ of work to their primary lab; 45% send <10% of work to a national lab. Primary reason for choosing lab: quality 41%, recommended by fellow dentist 22%, customer service 10%, price 3%. Turnaround received: 58% got 10–14 days.
findings.value: lab = 7–10% of overhead (58% of respondents); 60% drop labs for inconsistent work

findings.claim: Dandy 2022 Dental Industry Report: most practices partner with 2–3 labs; 84% use labs that specialize in specific products; 42% have lab relationships of 6+ years, 22% of 10+ years; self-reported remake rate with primary lab: 49% <5%, 21% 5–9%, 17% 10–14%, 12% 15–20%, 1% >20%
findings.detail: Vendor-sponsored survey; methodology not shown in the excerpt. Most practices use a local lab for primary work; aligners/retainers more likely from a secondary lab. Note 30% of respondents report remake rates of 10% or more, far above lab-side averages.
findings.value: 2–3 labs typical; 42% relationships 6+ yrs; 70% report remakes <10%

findings.claim: Dandy survey of 137 US dentists (Q3 2025, published Mar 2026): 94% have ordered a remake; 23% have remade a prosthetic 3+ times; 58% have or suspect they lost a patient due to a poor-fitting restoration
findings.detail: Attributed causes: inaccurate impressions/scans 34%, lab fabrication issues 31%, patient anatomy 12%. 42% say intraoral scanners reduced their remake rate. Vendor press release; small sample; treat directionally.
findings.value: 94% remakes; 58% lost a patient; 34% impression/scan error vs 31% lab error

findings.claim: LMT 2024 Remake Survey: average external remake rate by department: C&B 2.5%, implants 2.2%, complete dentures 2.8%, partials 3.6%, orthodontics 3.0%
findings.detail: Published in LMT's Q&A issue (Feb 2026). Companion LMT reports (Nov 2023, Feb 2024) state labs attribute on average 82% (>80%) of external remakes to dentist error, most often inadequate impressions and incorrect shades, consistent with LMT's 2011 and 2018 surveys; almost half of labs track remake percentages by client.
findings.value: C&B 2.5%; implants 2.2%; 82% attributed to dentist error

findings.claim: LMT lab poll (Nov 2023): two-thirds of labs offer milled restorations; of those, 45% scan and mill in-house, 34% own a scanner and outsource milling, 15% outsource the entire case, 6% outsource some milling
findings.detail: Among labs with in-house mills: 33% have one mill, 24% two, 17% three, 26% four or more. 42% say milling reduced their remake percentage. Relevant to Bear Milling: roughly a third of milling-offering labs are the scanner-but-no-mill outsourcing pool.
findings.value: 34% of labs outsource milling; 15% outsource whole case

findings.claim: ADA HPI Survey of Dental Practice 2025: average gross billings per private-practice GP $965,660; average GP net income $215,320 (specialists $1,213,040 / $346,520)
findings.detail: HPI publishes income, gross billings and total expenses but not a public breakdown of lab fees as a category (confirmed by secondary sources that note the category split is not in the open data). Third-party benchmarks for lab fees: 7–10% of collections (Dental Practice Insider, Mar 2026), 8–12% (rework.com citing Dental Economics 2023), 5.04% in the Dental Accounting Group 2024 CPA-client survey. A reciprocityaccounting.com reconstruction of ADA 2025 solo-GP data gives implied collections of ~$808k.

findings.claim: ESTIMATE: a typical GP owner spends roughly $40,000–$80,000 per year ($3,400–$6,700/month) on outside lab work
findings.detail: Basis: ADA-derived solo GP collections of ~$808k (2025) multiplied by the 5%–10% lab-fee range from DAG 2024 (5.04%) and third-party overhead benchmarks (7–10%). Crown-and-bridge or implant-heavy practices run higher (9–14% per rework.com). ADA does not publish the lab line directly, so this is an estimate, not a reported figure.

findings.claim: Digital impression (IOS) use among surveyed dentists rose to 57% in 2024 from 48% in 2023, ~50% in 2022 and 37% in 2020
findings.detail: Inside Dental Technology 'Trends in Dentistry 2025' compilation of practice surveys. A Journal of Periodontology review cites IOS ownership rising from 16% (2012) to 61% (2019) among GPs/prosthodontists. Dentistry IQ's 2013 survey had only 17% with IOS.

findings.claim: ESTIMATE: 10–20% of US general dentists own a chairside mill; no authoritative 2025 figure was found
findings.detail: Data points: Dentaltown 2023 self-selected poll, 23% 'already provide crowns in office' (n=105); DE/LMT 2013, chairside CAD/CAM a 'minority' with 63% neither owning nor planning; DPR 2024 Technology Census says chairside mills 'seem to have lost some of their appeal' while IOS and 3D printers grew (numbers in graphics not extracted); market-research claims range from ~12,450 US practices with in-office mills in 2025 (Exactitude, ~6% of ~200k practices) to 38% (pmarketresearch, not credible). Key Group Research's 2025 report measures '% dentist with a Milling System' but is paywalled.

findings.claim: DSO affiliation of US dentists rose from 7.2% (2015) to 16.1% (2024), and 30.7% of dentists 0–5 years out of school; US dental labs with payroll fell 25.8% from 6,865 (2013) to 5,096 (2023)
findings.detail: IDT 'Thriving in Times of Change' (Oct 2025) citing ADA HPI and Census data; HPI figures also summarized by elegantlab.com (Oct 2025). IDT quotes a lab owner: smaller labs are closing 'at a very alarming rate' with work picked up by other labs rather than M&A. IDT warns that long-standing clients may be lost as independent dentists join DSOs and are directed to preferred labs, and that DSO leadership 'wants data and pricing.'

findings.claim: NADL Spring 2025 member survey: 65% of US dental lab sales come from solo practices, 24% from small group practices, only 8% from DSOs/large groups
findings.detail: Reported in IDT Oct 2025. Indicates independent labs still depend overwhelmingly on independent dentists even as DSO share of dentists grows; DSOs negotiate aggressively on price and demand digital compatibility.

findings.claim: Heartland Dental (1,800+ offices, 3,000+ doctors) routes lab spend through 'Diamond Trusted Labs': 3 lab networks plus 6 single-location labs, 2 high-end aesthetic labs and 1 ortho lab; claims remakes under 3%, ~1 week in-lab turnaround, 40%+ savings for newly affiliated practices
findings.detail: Heartland's own page. LMT (Sep 2025) quotes Heartland's Dr. Todd Davis: ~1,000 Heartland doctors weren't doing dentures and those who did used local labs, spending about $190 more per arch than with Diamond Trusted Labs. Leixir Dental Laboratory Group's Heartland partnership was renewed through 2029 (Business Wire, May 15 2025); DDS Lab has been a Heartland partner since 2008; Heartland selected Dentira as enterprise lab-marketplace/routing platform (Dec 2025).

findings.claim: Aspen Dental (1,100+ locations) fabricates or repairs dentures in onsite labs and trained 1,300+ lab technicians for its Signature Elite denture rollout (Feb 2025); its in-house capacity is denture-focused, not crown-and-bridge
findings.detail: aspendental.com footnote: 'Dentures are either fully or partially fabricated or repaired using onsite labs... Some dentures may be fabricated in third-party labs.' Job postings describe a 'Denture Lab Technician' who oversees their own in-office laboratory. Full dentures advertised from $499/arch with a $49/yr savings plan.
findings.value: 1,300+ in-house lab techs; onsite denture labs

findings.claim: Glidewell opened BruxZir Express (Memphis, TN), a DSO-exclusive lab offering BruxZir crowns/bridges and occlusal appliances at special low rates, 3 days in lab, free-shipping options in the contiguous US and a 100% no-fault remake policy
findings.detail: Group Dentistry Now, Apr 4 2025. Glidewell also offers DSO pricing on Glidewell HT implants and Inclusive prosthetic components. Heartland calls itself 'the largest commercial buyer of dental supplies, equipment, and laboratory services in the United States' (Inside Dentistry, Jan 2024).

findings.claim: Glidewell dentist pricing (live price list): BruxZir Full-Strength $109 / $89 digital model-free; BruxZir Esthetic $119/$99; e.max posterior $129/$109, anterior $149/$129; Ti custom abutment $318/$298; BruxZir crown with custom abutment $454 (-$40 digital); BruxZir screw-retained $339 (-$20 digital)
findings.detail: Page undated; warranty page revised Sept 2025. In-lab working times: monolithic BruxZir 3 days; e.max 5 days (3 digital); custom abutment 8 days; abutment+crown 13 days; screw-retained 7 days. Next-Day BruxZir: digital model-free, scan by 2 p.m., receive 10:30 a.m. next day, free shipping. Digital savings: -$20/unit crowns, -$40 abutment+crown. Night guards: Comfort H/S $80, Comfort3D $90, CLEARsplint $104, soft $56. Older PDF price list and dealer mirrors (Riverside, Crown World) show identical numbers, indicating prices have been flat for several years.
findings.value: FCZ $89 digital; e.max $109 digital; SR implant crown $319 digital

findings.claim: Glidewell full-arch dentist pricing: Digital BruxZir Full-Arch Complete Service $2,795 (Esthetic $2,995); Copy Service $1,695; direct Mill Service from provided file $1,450 (Esthetic $1,650); analog Complete Service $3,433, or $4,150 with titanium bar; screw-retained hybrid denture with milled Ti bar $2,335; milled implant bar/framework $923
findings.detail: Complete service includes up to two provisional try-ins (extra try-ins $334, MUAs $116 each). Half payment due after first appointment. Full-arch in-lab times are on the Rx, not the price list. Integra's $1,700 monolithic arch is $1,095 below Complete Service but only $250 above Glidewell's mill-from-file price; Integra's $2,200 bar+superstructure is $135 below Glidewell's hybrid denture and $1,950 below Glidewell's zirconia-over-bar analog price.
findings.value: $2,795 digital complete; $1,450 mill-only; $4,150 with Ti bar

findings.claim: Glidewell shipping: FedEx Overnight $9 each way ($18 round trip per box, contiguous US) or free prepaid USPS Priority labels (2–4 business days each way); bundling multiple cases in one box waives inbound charges for additional cases; digital submission eliminates inbound shipping
findings.detail: glidewelldental.com pickup-and-delivery page dated 2026-05-05. Dandy's 2026 comparison table characterizes Glidewell as 'shipping fees apply' versus Dandy 'free'.

findings.claim: Glidewell warranty: BruxZir restorations (including over implants) and custom abutments warrantied for the life of the patient; screw-retained crowns/bridges and milled implant bars 7 years; dentures 1 year; no-fault remake within warranty period; Glidewell replaces any other lab's fractured single-unit monolithic zirconia crown free with BruxZir
findings.detail: Policy page 'Revised Form 4 – September 2025'. Liability capped at amount paid; no chair-time compensation; mandatory arbitration under California law.

findings.claim: Dandy pricing model: $1,000/month lab minimum for a free Dandy Vision scanner ('$30K value'), $2,500/month for a TRIOS 5 ('$39K value'); month-to-month; shortfall is billed as the difference; free remakes; lifetime warranty on fixed products; free shipping; 100% digital (no physical impressions); fixed work made in Utah, removables in Texas
findings.detail: Publicly stated per-unit prices: posterior zirconia 'from $99', dentures from $199/arch, surgical guides $109/site, night guards from $59 bundled with crowns, $64 diagnostic wax-ups (Dandy labs page); implant restoration $398 list all-in with custom abutment, crown, model, analog, screw (Dandy implant page, promo valid to Apr 30 2026). Third-party (Peak Dental Studio, May 2026): e.max and PFM from $125. Dandy's own 2024 implant comparison lists its $398 vs Glidewell $454, 14-day vs 13-day turnaround. Dandy claims '99% of Dandy practices once onboarded stay'. Full fee schedule is request-only.
findings.value: $1,000/mo min; zirconia from $99; implant crown $398; 5-day crowns

findings.claim: Dandy's reputation is mixed, not uniformly negative: Dentaltown's 2025 thread summary says it suits high-volume generalists (free scanner, reliable fits, live support) but critics cite scanner lock-in, limited STL export, rigid contracts/aggressive sales, mediocre esthetics and loss of lab choice; Google rating for the Lehi UT lab is 3.6/5 on 63 reviews
findings.detail: Dentaltown article (Jul 2025) and Howard Farran LinkedIn post (Jun 2025). Reddit r/Dentistry thread: one dentist reports Dandy implant crowns are 'ALWAYS tight' requiring 2–5 min adjustment; another reports a wrong-scan-body/wrong-connection sequence taking three attempts. PissedConsumer: 1.5/5 on 2 reviews (patients, lost flipper, delivery dates). Peak Dental Studio (May 2026) says the three most-cited reasons dentists leave Dandy are monthly minimums that don't fit volume, esthetic outcomes on complex cases, and wanting a named technician. Integra's report that Harmony Dental (Eugene OR) left Dandy after a bad experience is Integra's own account and was not independently verified.

findings.claim: Dandy's 2026 comparison table (its own marketing) lists standard crown turnaround including outbound shipping as Dandy 5 days, Glidewell 5 days, NDX 6 days, ROE 5 days, Keating 7 days, DDS Lab 12 days; warranties: Dandy lifetime all C&B, Glidewell lifetime zirconia only, NDX lifetime Verotek FCZ only, ROE 5-year zirconia, Keating 3-year, DDS Lab 1-year
findings.detail: Vendor-authored comparison; treat competitor entries as approximate. It also lists Dandy shipping 'Free' vs 'shipping fees apply' for Glidewell, DDS, Keating, ROE and 'vary' for NDX. Independent corroboration: ROE's own 2026 fee schedule shows 3 days in lab for model-free zirconia; Pro Arts (CA) lists 12 business days in lab; Peak Dental Studio lists 2 weeks.

findings.claim: Lab-to-lab zirconia crown mill-only pricing clusters at $18–$35 with free shipping at low thresholds: Monster Milling $19 (Honorzir HT+), Alien Milling $22 (Alien HT) / $34 (Multi-Layer 2.0), Haus Milling $18 (3M Lava Esthetic) / $35 (Haus ML Pro), K&A/Backup Milling $25–$29
findings.detail: Monster: 1-day turnaround for crown mill-only from STL (2 days with stain/glaze), no minimum, free ground on orders $90+, free 2-day $180+, free overnight $270+, first order free 2-day shipping; implant crown $35; Ti custom abutment from $65. Alien: implant crown $48; stain & glaze adds 1 day. Bear Milling's $22 zirconia mill-only is therefore at parity with Alien and $3 above Monster, with no scale, shipping-threshold or turnaround advantage demonstrated.

findings.claim: Lab-to-lab full-arch zirconia from STL: Monster $580 (Honorzir) / $770 (Aizir ML) / $880 (3Dpro), Alien $649 (HT) / $849 (ML 2.0) / $1,049 (Extreme), K&A/Backup $650–$750, Mabel copy-mill $999, Glidewell dentist-facing mill-from-file $1,450; Bear's $650 is mid-pack
findings.detail: Monster turnaround: full-arch zirconia 4 days from STL; Bar + full zirconia 5 days. Alien full-arch stain & glaze with pink gingiva adds 3 days. Alien PMMA full arch $449; Monster full-arch PMMA 3 days.

findings.claim: Lab-to-lab titanium bars: Alien $399 flat regardless of implant count (MUA interfaces only), Monster $350 flat (+$280 design from model scan or +$400 from IOS; MUAs $18/unit), Ivorymade $650/arch, Mabel $699 (bar/framework to master model); dentist-facing: ROE $825, Glidewell $923; Bear's $299 std / $399 rush is at the low end
findings.detail: Alien iBar (Ti bar + zirconia overlay, split by Alien) $869 sale / $1,169 list; Monster Bar&Zir $950–$1,350. Argen Digital: Ti and CoCr bars and Ti abutments ship in 2 business days (3 pm PST cut-off) but prices are login-only. Straumann CARES centralized production brochure (NAMLIT_1223) lists Ti CARES abutment $199, ZrO2 abutment $316, Variobase $129.

findings.claim: Mabel Dental Lab (Ohio) Jan 2026 lab-to-lab price list is a full outsourcing benchmark: full-contour zirconia $59 (coping $39), e.max $69, Ti custom abutment $119, screw-retained full zirconia $189, zirconia full-arch implant prosthesis $1,999 (incl. up to 6 MUAs and 2 try-ins), copy-mill full-arch $999, CAD/CAM Ti bar $699, screw-retained hybrid denture $1,299, zirconia over hybrid bar $2,999, night guard hard/soft $65; 6 in-lab days digital; shipping $9 each way
findings.detail: Shows that a finished lab-to-lab arch (not mill-only) runs ~$2,000 and a bar+zirconia ~$3,000, versus Integra's dentist-facing $1,700 and $2,200. Mabel's Oct 2025 list is identical, indicating no price movement.

findings.claim: National-network labs operate inside Integra's home market: NDX Issaquah (640 NW Gilman Blvd, Issaquah WA 98027, 'digital design and on-site milling'), NDX Advanced Dental Technologies (11820 NE Crestwood Dr, Vancouver WA), Modern Dental Center Seattle (330 112th Ave NE Ste 101, Bellevue WA 98004), MicroDental Northwest (1123 N Grant Pl, Kennewick WA)
findings.detail: Modern Dental Center Seattle is in the same city as Integra; it offers case planning, custom shade matching and technical support (manager Julian Infante, CDT). NDX's only published price data found is a 2020 Elite Dental Alliance network schedule for NDX Pacific (CA): full/solid zirconia $49 ($44 IOS modeless), e.max $69, no shipping fees on fixed cases, next-day air delivery, $25/unit 4-day rush. NDX Pacific states NDX serves 'over 30,000 dentists each year'. Current NDX/Modern retail pricing is not public.

findings.claim: DDS Lab (Tampa) United Concordia network schedule (document references Feb 1, 2025 alloy policy): zirconia solid $69 ($64 digital), zirconia HT $70, lithium disilicate $75 ($64 digital), temp crown $32, shipping $6.99/case, night guard hard $70 / soft $50, rush $150/unit; Dandy's table lists DDS at 12-day turnaround and 1-year warranty
findings.detail: This is an insurer-network discount schedule, not DDS Lab's standard retail list, which was not found publicly. DDS Lab is a Heartland Diamond Trusted Lab since 2008. The schedule also shows implant package lines ($299/unit titanium hybrid denture up to five implants, $380/unit six-plus, $199/unit full-arch solid zirconia) whose per-unit basis is unclear from the extract.

findings.claim: ROE Dental Lab (Ohio) 2026 fee schedule (REV100726) is a well-run digital-lab comp: zRc zirconia $93 model-free (3 days), TLZ zirconia $122, e.max $134; TLZ-SR screw-retained crown $299 model-free (4 days); Ti/Zr abutment + TLZ crown $411 model-free (7 days); TLZ-IB coping-free full-arch zirconia final $2,420 (10 days); titanium bar $825 (11 days); CLEARguard splints $69–$111; tax and shipping not included
findings.detail: ROE also sells photogrammetry design services ($287–$335) and a prepaid full-arch package $2,520. Shows a reputable mid-size lab pricing its monolithic arch $720 above Integra and its Ti bar $526 above Bear's standard bar.
findings.value: zirconia $93; SR crown $299; full-arch $2,420; Ti bar $825

findings.claim: Low-price national shippers targeting the Pacific Northwest: Next Dental Lab (Deerfield Beach FL) advertises $39 zirconia, $47 e.max, All-on-X with Ti bar from $1,795 to Oregon practices with ~4 business days ground each way and prepaid labels, and claims typical Oregon lab fees of $100–$185 for a zirconia crown; TrueGuide Lab (NJ) lists $99 zirconia, $139 e.max, $349 SR crown on Ti-base, $399 custom abutment + crown, All-on-X from $2,999, 5–7 business days, free ground on 3+ units
findings.detail: Next Dental Lab's 'typical Oregon fee' range is its own marketing estimate, not survey data. Both illustrate that cross-country ground shipping (4 days each way) is the main friction for ultra-low-price labs, which is the window Integra's local turnaround can exploit.

findings.claim: Milling-center pricing that is NOT public: Argen Digital (San Diego; 140,000 sq ft, 150 machines, 2-business-day Ti abutments/bars), Core3dcentres USA (Las Vegas), Jensen Dental, Zahn/Henry Schein, Preat (patient-specific bars), Panthera Dental (Quebec; Fusion Bar with split overlay STL), Zirkonzahn (components with up to 30-year warranty), Evolve Dentistry (pricing page removed), DLMS and ProtoDent (no price pages found); Strategy Milling (Leetsdale PA) publishes only its gold milling fee of $29.95/unit plus alloy and claims an external remake rate below 0.5%
findings.detail: Hiossen Digital Center (Dec 2025 list): SmartFit Ti custom abutment $190 list / $119 with implant package. Digital Dental (Scottsdale AZ) milling center: 2-day abutments/crowns, 5-day full arch, prices not listed.

findings.claim: Oral Arts (Huntsville AL) historical 2017 Smile Source schedule: Element-Z solid zirconia $99, e.max $99, crown with custom Ti/Zr abutment $368, model-less screw-retained crown $248, 5-day standard turnaround, free shipping both ways; current pricing not published
findings.detail: Historical network pricing; useful only as a floor for a free-shipping national lab. Burbank Dental Lab, Sun Dental Labs, Bayshore Dental Studio (dentist-owned, Tampa, 'individualized pricing' for groups), ProSmile, Dental Lab Direct and Absolute Dental Services publish no fee schedules; Burbank and Bayshore require a request.

unknowns: Dandy's complete per-unit fee schedule and turnaround table (request-only); only 'from $99' zirconia, $398 implant restoration list, $199/arch dentures, $109 guides and $59 bundled night guards are public.

Current standard (non-network) retail fee schedules for NDX labs (incl. NDX Issaquah), Modern Dental Center Seattle, MicroDental Northwest, DDS Lab, Burbank Dental Lab, Sun Dental Labs, Bayshore Dental Studio, ProSmile, Dental Lab Direct and Absolute Dental Services: none are published; DDS Lab's public document is a United Concordia network schedule and NDX's is a 2020 alliance schedule.

Lab-to-lab prices from Argen Digital, Core3dcentres, Jensen Dental, Zahn/Henry Schein, Preat, Panthera, Zirkonzahn, Evolve Dentistry (pricing page removed), DLMS and ProtoDent: login/quote only or not found.
Whether Harmony Dental (Eugene OR) actually left Dandy and why: Integra's own account, not independently verified.

Share of US general dentists owning a chairside mill in 2025: no authoritative figure found (estimate 10–20%); Key Group Research 2025 report measures it but is paywalled; DPR 2024 census values are in graphics not extracted.
ADA HPI lab-fee share of GP expenses: HPI does not publish the category split in open data; third-party benchmarks range 5%–12% of collections.
Glidewell in-lab working times for full-arch services (listed only on Rx forms, not the price list).
Exact interpretation of DDS Lab's UC schedule full-arch lines ($299/$380/$199 'per unit').
LMT 2019 survey sample size and demographics (link not fetched).
Whether NDX Issaquah mills zirconia in-house at scale (page says 'on-site milling' without detail).
Remaining WebSearch budget was zero for this task; all discovery used Exa search, which may have missed pages indexed only by Google/Bing.
